facts.value: The Common Agricultural Policy (CAP) is the agricultural policy of the European Union. It implements a system of agricultural subsidies and other programmes.
The EEC budget cost reduced from 73% in 1985 to 37% in 2017.
The Common Agricultural Policy has been criticised on the grounds of its cost and its environmental and humanitarian effects.
The Common Fisheries Policy (CFP) is the fisheries policy of the European Union.

The Common Fisheries Policy sets quotas for which member states are allowed to catch each type of fish, as well as encouraging the fishing industry by various market interventions and fishing subsidies.

The Common Fisheries Policy was introduced in 2009 with the Treaty of Lisbon, which formally enshrined fisheries conservation policy as one of the few 'exclusive competences' reserved for the European Union.
